content: Fenofibrate is prescribed to help reduce the levels of cholesterol and triglycerides (fatty substances) in your blood. It is used in conjunction with dietary changes, such as reducing cholesterol and fat intake. The accumulation of cholesterol and fats along the walls of your arteries, a condition known as atherosclerosis, can restrict blood flow and reduce the oxygen supply to your heart, brain, and other parts of your body. By lowering your blood levels of cholesterol and fats, fenofibrate may help prevent heart disease, angina (chest pain), strokes, and heart attacks. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Fenofibrate is available as a capsule to be taken orally, usually once a day with a meal. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take fenofibrate exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. Continue taking fenofibrate even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before taking fenofibrate, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to fenofibrate or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially anticoagulants (blood thinners) like warfarin (Coumadin), HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors (cholesterol-lowering agents) such as lovastatin (Mevacor), pravastatin (Pravachol), and simvastatin (Zocor), cholestyramine (Questran), cyclosporine (Sandimmune, Neoral), and any vitamins or herbal products. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had heart disease, gallbladder disease, or liver or kidney disease. Additionally, let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking fenofibrate, contact your doctor immediately. While taking fenofibrate, adhere to a low-cholesterol, low-fat diet. This includes foods such as cottage cheese, fat-free milk, fish, vegetables, poultry, egg whites, and polyunsaturated oils and margarines (e.g., corn, safflower, canola, and soybean oils). Avoid foods high in fat, such as meat (especially liver and fatty cuts), egg yolks, whole milk, cream, butter, shortening, pastries, cakes, cookies, gravy, peanut butter, chocolate, olives, potato chips, coconut, cheese (other than cottage cheese), coconut oil, palm oil, and fried foods. If you miss a dose of fenofibrate, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Fenofibrate may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: gas, headache, stomach pain, upset stomach, dizziness or lightheadedness, constipation, fatigue, or a runny nose. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: weakness, muscle pain or tenderness, joint pain, rash, infection, or flu-like symptoms. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store fenofibrate in the container it came in, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and the laboratory. Your doctor will order specific laboratory tests to monitor your response to fenofibrate. Do not share your medication with anyone else. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
